title: Auth0 vs FullStory: Identity Management vs Digital Experience Analytics
description: A practical decision guide to Auth0 and FullStory. Auth0 focuses on authentication and identity workflows for applications; FullStory focuses on understanding user interactions and digital product experiences. Compare each product against its intended workflow instead of relying on unsupported star ratings or a universal winner. Verify current features, availability, and terms with the vendors.

verdict: Authentication and digital-experience analytics have different purposes. An application may use an identity platform to control access and an analytics product to understand how users interact with the interface, subject to privacy and consent requirements. Compare current vendor terms, implementation effort, privacy/security requirements, integrations, data portability, and ongoing ownership before purchasing. This page does not claim an independently conducted benchmark or establish a universal winner.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Auth0 and FullStory?
faqs.answer: Auth0 focuses on authentication and identity workflows for applications; FullStory focuses on understanding user interactions and digital product experiences. They are evaluated against different core workflows, so begin with the outcome your team needs.

faqs.question: Can Auth0 replace FullStory?
faqs.answer: Do not assume so. List the capabilities and controls you currently rely on in FullStory, then test whether Auth0 can meet each requirement without creating operational or governance gaps.

faqs.question: Can a team use Auth0 and FullStory together?
faqs.answer: Potentially, if both workflows are needed. Define which product owns each step, what information should be shared, who controls access, and how errors or changes are handled.

faqs.question: How should I compare the costs?
faqs.answer: Compare current vendor quotes for your actual scope, including seats or usage, required features, implementation, integrations, training, support, renewals, and staff time.

faqs.question: What should I test before deciding?
faqs.answer: Use a representative task and realistic data. Record completion time, missing capabilities, administration effort, permissions, export options, and whether each product supports the workflow it is intended to serve.
